details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/provider_outage.py:725-728 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_resume` closes outage markers even when recovery operations failed, preventing later ticks from retrying the failed work.
  WHY: Once the marker is closed, subsequent ticks find no open outage to resume; one reviewer rated this major rather than blocker.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:594-596, 696 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Recovery filters PRs by `updated_at` against a window starting at the outage marker's `created_at`, which can exclude the PRs that failed before the marker was created.
  WHY: The triggering PR can be skipped on every recovery tick; one reviewer rated this major rather than blocker.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:272-273 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: An editor-summary comment can replace the latest review outcome without verifying that it belongs to the current head SHA.
  WHY: A summary for a different head can cause `is_resume_candidate()` to reject the paused PR during recovery.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:624 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The hold-release path treats a PR as conflicted only when `mergeable_state` is exactly `"dirty"`.
  WHY: Other non-clean states such as `"blocked"`, `"behind"`, or `"unknown"` can be treated as conflict-free, releasing a hold on a PR that may not be ready for review.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:5052-5078 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The empty-noop branch does not export the provider-unavailable flags and posts the generic retry comment instead of the paused-provider comment.
  WHY: Downstream guards and comment handling do not recognize the outage in this branch; a reviewer rated this major rather than blocker.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1398-1427 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Reviewer logs and `status_*.txt` files share a sorted list and total byte budget, so large logs can consume the budget before status files are read.
  WHY: A successful reviewer status may be missed, allowing a 429/5xx log line to cause a false provider-outage classification.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:109-110 | severity=major | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job does not check `inputs.dry_run` on manual dispatch.
  WHY: A dry-run dispatch can still perform live recovery mutations.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:525-571 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `record` calls can each create and retain an outage marker when an eventually consistent listing shows only their own issue.
  WHY: Both calls can report `action=created` and send an alert, leaving duplicate open markers.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:103-167 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job has no concurrency group preventing overlapping probe and resume executions.
  WHY: Overlapping ticks can duplicate review dispatches, cleanup operations, resume comments, and recovery alerts.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:620-625 | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The hold-release gate rejects a hold when any failed check run has a missing or malformed `details_url`.
  WHY: A run that cannot be mapped to a workflow run ID can leave an outage-only hold in place and prevent recovery.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:664-689 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A persistently failing provider probe has no max-age or bail-out path.
  WHY: A misconfigured model or unavailable API key can leave review dispatches paused indefinitely without an alert beyond the initial one.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:607-611, 725-726 | severity=major | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Resume work is dispatched before its handled keys are persisted in the resume comment.
  WHY: If later work or the comment post fails, a subsequent tick can dispatch the same PRs again.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:138 | severity=major | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The probe step defaults `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` to `'true'` for in-repository redispatches, bypassing an operator setting of `false`.
  WHY: A paused PR can be redispatched with workflow edits enabled despite the operator's opt-out.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:103-167 | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The sweep relies on the `skip_review_dispatch` fallback when the probe job is skipped, rather than an explicit job-level output.
  WHY: The reported behavior currently works through the fallback, but removing it could leave the sweep with an empty input.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:538-555 | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Probe error details may include an unredacted request URL in logs.
  WHY: The detail is operator-visible and could expose query parameters if they are added to the request URL.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:458 | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A quoted fixer-handoff marker in a comment can be interpreted as an actual hand-off.
  WHY: A matching marker in a code block can cause the resume logic to skip the PR.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:510-524 | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `parse_time` does not guard against future-dated timestamps when applying the outage window.
  WHY: Clock skew can allow a label applied before the outage to match the window and be removed.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:110 | severity=nit | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The probe job's timeout bound can still consume runner time if the probe hangs at the network level.
  WHY: A network-level hang can use the job's runner budget until the job timeout fires.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:153-158 | severity=nit | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The probe can make an OpenRouter call even when a GitHub marker-list read has failed.
  WHY: The probe call incurs a small additional cost during an incident with GitHub API rate limits.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:788-814 | severity=nit | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `build_parser()` does not register the planned `status` subcommand.
  WHY: An operator invoking `provider_outage.py status` receives an invalid-choice error; the plan-text drift is the main issue rather than a runtime defect.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Every new tracked script in `scripts/` must be listed in `docs/INVENTORY.md` under the Scripts section.
  expected_change_site: `docs/INVENTORY.md`, `## Scripts` section
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `scripts/provider_outage.py` is absent from the PR diff's inventory changes; the reviewers report that `tests/inventory_parity.py` will report the missing script and CI will fail.
- requirement: The empty-noop branch must export `AUTOFIX_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE=true` and `AUTOFIX_PROVIDER_OUTAGE` when the reason is `provider_unavailable`, and post the paused-provider comment.
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, "Post editor summary comment" step, empty-noop branch
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The branch extracts only `marker=`, does not export either provider variable, posts the generic retry comment, and sets `AUTOFIX_EDITOR_EMPTY_NOOP=true`, which skips the later paused-provider comment step.
- requirement: The plan specifies CLI subcommands `record`, `status`, and `tick` for `scripts/provider_outage.py`.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `build_parser()`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `build_parser()` registers `record` and `tick` but does not register `status`; the plan and PR do not document the omission as a deviation.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `Line or code reference: 727-728`
  PROBLEM: `_resume` closes every outage marker even when `summary["errors"]` contains failures.
  WHY: Failed consumer-repo or PR recovery work can be stranded because subsequent ticks find no open marker.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `Line or code reference: 696 (`window_start = parse_time(primary.get("created_at")) or now`) and 594-596 (`updated < window_start`)`
  PROBLEM: The recovery window begins at the marker's creation time but filters PRs by `updated_at`.
  WHY: The triggering PR may have been updated before marker creation and be skipped during recovery.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `Line or code reference: 272-273 (`if _EDITOR_SUMMARY_TEXT in body: latest = {"kind": "summary"}`)`
  PROBLEM: An editor-summary comment can become the latest review outcome without being checked against the current head SHA.
  WHY: A summary for a different head can override the current head's provider-unavailable failure and cause recovery to skip the PR.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `Line or code reference: 624 (`conflicted=pull.get("mergeable_state") == "dirty"`)`
  PROBLEM: Only `"dirty"` triggers the conflicted guard during hold release.
  WHY: Other unclean or unknown merge states can be treated as conflict-free and have their outage hold released.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `Line or code reference: 607-611` vs `725-726`
  PROBLEM: Handled keys are persisted only after inline resume dispatches complete.
  WHY: A failure before the resume comment is posted can leave already-dispatched PRs unrecorded and subject to redispatch.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, `Line or code reference: 1398-1427`
  PROBLEM: Reviewer logs and status files share an alphabetical read order and a total byte budget.
  WHY: Large logs can exhaust the budget before status files are read, causing a successful reviewer run to be misclassified as a provider outage.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`, `Line or code reference: 109-110`
  PROBLEM: The probe job condition does not check `inputs.dry_run`.
  WHY: A manual dry-run dispatch can execute live recovery mutations.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
